chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-'Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hadd (fixed penalty) of the Luti (sodomist) is like the Hadd of the Zani (adulterer/fornicator). And he said: If he was Muhsan (married), he is stoned, and otherwise he is whipped.'

key_terms.اللُّوطِيِّ: Al-Luti (sodomist, from the story of Lot)

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadd penalty for sodomy in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the fixed legal penalty (Hadd) for sodomy (Luti) is equivalent to that of general sexual misconduct (Zani), grounding this in the principle of analogy (Qiyas) within Shia jurisprudence. He clarifies that if the person is Muhsan (married), the penalty is stoning (Rajm), whereas if unmarried, it is flogging (Jild), reflecting the standard application of marital status to sexual offenses in Islamic law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahi, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’ala Bin Al Fazeyl who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The Penalty (Hadd) of the sodomist is like the Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer’. And heasws said: ‘If he was married, would be stoned, or else whipped’.
